text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
*Pilots lodge court appeal against TAP-Air Portugal's order to return to work. Pilots' union considers move unconstitutional and illegal.
*Portugal's five largest banks to inject 20 billion escudos into soon-to-be-launched new Fund for the Internationalisation of Portuguese Companies.
*Opposition leader Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa says minority Socialist government "must last" until 1999 when its four-year term ends.
*TAP "in coma" as number of pilots call in sick after government attempts to break partial strike with its order to return to normal working.
*Investment in Expo '98, the World Fair to be held in Lisbon next year, reaches 240 billion escudos in 1997.
*Government sets up new construction company - JAE-Construcao to stimulate planned road building projects, a source at the Planning Ministry says.
*Algarve tourist areas had better July with room occupation rising 3.45 percent compared with the same period last year.
